input: Apply for a foreign language teaching assistant program

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: There are many distinct programs (Fulbright ETA, TAPIF, CIEE, JET, etc.) each with different requirements, timelines, and application components — knowing which one narrows every other decision.
The target country or region determines language requirements, visa steps, and cultural fit sections of the application.
The user's current status (student, recent graduate, working professional) affects eligibility, recommender choices, and how to frame their experience.
The application deadline directly dictates urgency, pacing, and what can realistically be completed in time.
Knowing which application materials are already in hand versus still needed (transcripts, language test scores, recommendations) determines the immediate next action.
The user's priorities — e.g., emphasising teaching experience, language fluency, or cultural exchange — shape how personal statements and essays should be framed.
Understanding what a strong application looks like to the user (first-choice program acceptance vs. any offer) determines how selective and thorough the preparation needs to be.

gold.taskTitle: Apply for a foreign language teaching assistant program
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to apply to a program where they will serve as a foreign language teaching assistant, likely abroad or at an institution requiring a structured application.

questions.title: Which specific program are you applying to?
questions.description: Identify the exact program (e.g., Fulbright ETA, TAPIF, JET, CIEE) so requirements and components can be scoped accurately.

questions.title: Which country or region do you want to teach in?
questions.description: Pinpoint the target country or region, which determines language requirements, visa logistics, and relevant cultural sections of the application.

questions.title: What is your current status — student, graduate, or professional?
questions.description: Clarify the user's academic or professional standing to assess eligibility and how to frame qualifications and recommenders.

questions.title: When is the application deadline you are working toward?
questions.description: Establish the hard deadline to set a realistic pace and determine urgency for each application component.

questions.title: Which application materials do you already have ready?
questions.description: Identify what is already complete (transcripts, language scores, letters of recommendation) versus what still needs to be gathered or created.

questions.title: What experience or quality do you most want to highlight?
questions.description: Understand whether the user wants to foreground teaching experience, language fluency, cultural immersion, or another strength to guide personal statement framing.

questions.title: Is this your top-choice program or one of several you are pursuing?
questions.description: Determine whether the user is aiming exclusively at one program or building a broader application strategy, which affects how thorough and selective the preparation needs to be.
